data.title: The Cat Can Stay

premise.hero_want: Noor wants to welcome a hot cat that pads into the courtyard.
premise.problem: The cat is hot and pants in the sun.
premise.mechanism: Noor gets a dish, then she and Mum fill it at the outdoor tap so the cat can drink.
premise.resolution: The cat cools down, plays and settles beside Noor.

key_objects.name: Dish
key_objects.description: A shallow blue ceramic dish for the cat.

key_objects.name: Tap
key_objects.description: A simple brass tap fixed to the courtyard wall.

data.cold_read: A clear, warm visitor story at the exemplar level: Noor notices the cat’s need, decides to welcome it and leads the simple dish-and-tap solution. The story has one connected location, one adult, two key objects and one familiar mechanism. The phonics contract is met, including four distinct “ay” words and the required 2+4 read_words split. Only two minor line-and-scene refinements are needed.

issues.detail: The scene has Noor set the empty dish beside the cat, only for her to take it to the tap on the next page. This unnecessary back-and-forth is removed by showing Noor carrying the dish towards the tap.
“It is not hot” sounds like a blunt caption and makes the change feel instant. “It rests in the cool spot” is more natural while keeping the same simple resolution.
